attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his signed post, published 2024-06-11. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The sentence says there was an AI bubble and that Altman inflated it, which is a causal claim. The forecast in the same sentence, that he will push OpenAI into more industries, is a separate claim and correctly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: speculative excess in AI by June 2024, with Altman a material contributor but not the only cause. Zitron gave no measure, so the result depends on that reading. The contract correctly flags this.

evidence.note: Stanford AI Index (April 2024): overall private AI investment fell while generative AI investment rose about ninefold in 2023. It shows investment growth, not overvaluation, and says nothing about Altman's role.
Sequoia (Sept 2023) warns that GPU capacity is being overbuilt. This is one investor's modelled concern about future revenue, not established overvaluation. It does not mention Altman.

New Yorker (April 2026) says Altman's rhetoric helped sustain OpenAI's cash burn and that experts warn of a bubble. It describes a later period and does not separate out his contribution to any excess by June 2024.

reviews.rationale: None of the evidence establishes speculative overvaluation by June 2024 or separates out Altman's material contribution. Stanford shows only investment trends. Sequoia gives a modelled overbuild risk. The New Yorker piece describes a later period. Nothing in the packet directly contradicts the claim either, so the outcome is unresolved.
